chunks: Allah has not been worshipped by anything like al-Bada'.
And in a narration of Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Allah has not been glorified with the likes of al-Bada'.

key_terms.البداء: al-Bada': The doctrine that God can change His decrees; a key Shia theological concept affirming divine sovereignty and responsiveness to human action
key_terms.عُبِدَ: Passive form of 'ibada (worship); the text states God has not been 'worshipped' (i.e., no act of worship equals acknowledging al-Bada')
key_terms.عُظِّمَ: Passive form of ta'dhim (glorification/reverence); the alternate narration uses glorification language rather than worship

ai.seo_question: What is al-Bada' and why is it important in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that al-Bada'—the doctrine that God can alter His pre-ordained decrees according to human actions—is the highest form of worship and glorification of God. In Shia theology, al-Bada' affirms God's absolute freedom and ongoing creative sovereignty: He is not bound by previous decrees and can update them based on new realities such as a person's prayers, repentance, or charity. For Zurara's early audience, this concept was revolutionary—it meant God remains actively involved in the world and can respond to human supplication, making acts of worship meaningful and consequential.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Ahmad Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al Hajjal, from Abu Is’haq Sa’alba, from Zurara Bin Ayn, 
(It has been narrated) from one of the two (5<sup>th</sup> or 6<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>) having said: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> has not been worshipped by anything like The Changing of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>’s Decision (الْبَدَاءِ)’.

And in another report of Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Salim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> (having said): ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> has not been revered with the likes of The Changing of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>’s Decision (الْبَدَاءِ)’.
en.sarwar: 1. It is narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from al-Hajjal from abu Ishaq Tha‘laba from Zurara ibn A‘yun from one of the two Imams who has said the following. “Allah is best worshipped with belief in al-Bada’.
In another Hadith from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hisham ibn Salim from abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) who has said, “Allah’s Greatness is not realized as good as it is realized with belief in al-Bad.”
